name: Buttermilk Vanilla Waffles

instructions.primary_message: For the Batter: In a large bowl, combine flour, powdered sugar, salt, baking soda, baking powder, and scrapings of one large vanilla bean, mixing by hand until the seeds are well dispersed. Add buttermilk, melted butter, egg whites, and vanilla extract and whisk until smooth.

For the Waffles: Set waffle iron to medium and preheat until indicator is ready. For an 20-cm square machine, scrape in roughly half the batter. For a 18-cm Belgian machine, scrape in about one-third. Close lid and cook until waffle is golden brown but still steaming, 4 1/2 to 6 minutes depending on the depth and heat of your machine. Serve immediately, with copious amounts of maple syrup, and griddle remaining batter as before.

schema_metadata.keywords: baking, breakfast, brunch, buttermilk, easy, one bowl, quick, waffle

description: With only a pinch of baking soda to help them brown, these waffles are leavened primarily by steam, so they're light and crisp, with a hint of tangy goodness.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Maple syrup, for serving

Notes: From size and depth to heat settings and materials (cast iron versus nonstick), waffle irons vary considerably from brand to brand; a small test waffle is a low-risk way to determine how the batter behaves on your machine.
In place of buttermilk, this recipe can be made with a 50/50 blend of plain, nonfat Greek yogurt and milk. You can also make this recipe without the vanilla bean, but the waffles won't be as aromatic.
author: Stella Parks
